fields.name: Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī
fields.aka: Gadādhara Paṇḍit Gosvāmī, Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Paṇḍita Prabhu, Paṇḍita Gosāñi, Gadāi, Gadādhara Ṭhākura, Gadhadara Paṇḍit Gosvāmī
fields.appearance: Vaiśākha amāvasyā, 1408 Śaka (1486 CE) (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna; Gauḍīya calendar)
fields.disappearance: Jyaiṣṭha amāvasyā, 1456 Śaka, in Purī, at 47, eleven months after Lord Caitanya (Abhidhāna); the Gauḍīya calendar, counting months from full moon to full moon, keeps this new moon in Āṣāḍha (Vāmana)
fields.place: Born at Beliṭi, Chittagong (Jayakṛṣṇa dāsa: Śrīhaṭṭa); from his 13th year in Navadvīpa, at his maternal uncle's house; later in Purī, serving Ṭoṭā-Gopīnātha at Yameśvara
fields.guru: Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi (dīkṣā; in Purī he took the mantra from him a second time)
fields.disciples: Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, Acyutānanda (son of Advaita), Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī, Ananta Ācārya, Bhāgavatācārya (Raghunātha Paṇḍita), Nayanānanda Miśra, Madhu Paṇḍita, Maṅgala Vaiṣṇava, Vallabha-caitanya dāsa, Puruṣottama Jānā, Vallabha Bhaṭṭa, Uddhava dāsa, Dhruvānanda, Śrīdhara Brahmacārī, Haridāsa Brahmacārī, Vāṇīnātha, Bhāgavata dāsa, Amogha Paṇḍita, Lakṣmīnātha Paṇḍita, Śrīnātha Cakravartī, Puṣpa-gopāla, Yadu Gāṅgulī and the others of his branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.79–86; fifty-six in the Abhidhāna)
fields.notes:
One of the Pañca-tattva: the Lord's pleasure potency (īśa-śakti). Father: Mādhava Miśra; mother: Ratnāvatī Devī; younger brother: Vāṇīnātha (father of Nayanānanda); grandfather: Vilāsa Ācārya of Beliṭi. A Vārendra brāhmaṇa of the Kāśyapa gotra; a lifelong brahmacārī. In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, with Lalitā entering him (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 147-153).

Studied Īśvara Purī's Kṛṣṇa-līlāmṛta; took dīkṣā from Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi after doubting him (Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 7.44-112) and the mantra again in Purī (Antya 10.22-27; Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 16.78). Kṣetra-sannyāsa in Purī, served Ṭoṭā-Gopīnātha and read the Bhāgavatam to the Lord; gave the mantra to Vallabha Bhaṭṭa with the Lord's permission (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 7). The Lord wrote a verse in his Gītā; he left it, with Gopīnātha, to Nayanānanda (Prema-vilāsa).

Dates and place from the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna (entry «Gadādhara Paṇḍita»), which agrees with B. V. Tīrtha, «Sri Chaitanya: His Associates» (the English text of the record gives 1534 CE for his disappearance).

fields.name: Śrī Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi
fields.place: Zamindar of Cakraśālā, Chittagong; family home at Mekhalā near Hāṭ-hazārī (Śrīla Prabhupāda also names Bāghiyā near Dacca); also had a house in Navadvīpa
fields.notes:
Father: Bāṇeśvara Brahmacārī (some write Śuklāmbara Brahmacārī); mother: Gaṅgā Devī; wife: Ratnāvatī (Kīrtidā). A Vārendra brāhmaṇa; a friend of Mādhava Miśra, Gadādhara's father, and an intimate friend of Svarūpa Dāmodara. Lord Caitanya called him «father» and named him Premanidhi. Lived like a prince; Gadādhara doubted him, then took dīkṣā from him (Caitanya-bhāgavata Madhya 7). In Purī Jagannātha and Balarāma slapped him in a dream for criticising the starched cloth of the Oḍana-ṣaṣṭhī (Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 10; Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 16.76-81). His Lakṣmī-Govinda deities are still at his birthplace; the thirteenth generation of his family lives at Mekhalā (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Vṛṣabhānu, Rādhā's father (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 54-57).

The Abhidhāna and the Gauḍīya calendar give no date of disappearance.

fields.name: Vallabha Bhaṭṭa (Vallabhācārya)
fields.aka: Vallabha Ācārya, Vallabhācārya, Vallabha Bhaṭṭa, Vallabha
fields.appearance: 1479, at Campāraṇya (another text: Vaiśākha kṛṣṇa ekādaśī, 1499)
fields.disappearance: Āṣāḍha śukla dvitīyā, 1531, at Hanumān-ghāṭ, Kāśī (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna; another text: the full moon of Āṣāḍha)
fields.place: Born at Campāraṇya (Madhya Pradesh); lived at Āḍāila near Prayāga; Gokula; died at Hanumān-ghāṭ, Kāśī
fields.guru: Gadādhara Paṇḍita (mantra of Kiśora-gopāla, with Lord Caitanya's permission); earlier a follower of Viṣṇusvāmī
fields.disciples: Pūrṇamalla; his sons Gopīnātha and Viṭṭhalanātha
fields.works: Brahma-sūtra-aṇubhāṣya; Subodhinī (on the Bhāgavatam); Tattvārtha-dīpa-nibandha; Ṣoḍaśa-grantha; Śikṣā-śloka; Śruti-gītā; Mathurā-māhātmya; Madhurāṣṭaka; Puruṣottama-nāma-sahasra; Parivṛḍhāṣṭaka; Nandakumārāṣṭaka; Pañca-ślokī; Gāyatrī-bhāṣya (84 works in his sampradāya)
fields.notes:
Founder of the Vallabhī sampradāya (Puṣṭi-mārga, Śuddhādvaita). Son of Lakṣmaṇa Bhaṭṭa and Illammāgāru (Sallamagaru), Telugu brāhmaṇas of the Bhāradvāja gotra. Received Lord Caitanya at Āḍāila (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 19); in Purī his pride was humbled and he took the mantra of Kiśora-gopāla from Gadādhara Paṇḍita, leaving the worship of Bāla-gopāla; his followers kept the old way (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Antya 7; Abhidhāna). Set up Mādhavendra Purī's Gopāla again on Govardhana. In Gadādhara's branch: «Vallabha Bhaṭṭa, resident of Āyarola» (Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 56). Not the Vallabhācārya who was the father of Lakṣmīpriyā.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Śukadeva Gosvāmī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 110).

Disappearance from the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna (Āṣāḍha śukla dvitīyā); the record had the full moon of Āṣāḍha.

fields.name: Bhāgavatācārya (Raghunātha Paṇḍita)
fields.aka: Bhāgavata Ācārya, Raghunātha Paṇḍita, Raghunātha Bhaṭṭācārya, Bhāgavata (Raghunātha Bhaṭṭācārya)
fields.place: Varāhanagara (Māli-pāḍā, the Pāṭbāḍī), north of Calcutta
fields.works: Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prema-taraṅgiṇī (Bengali verse rendering of the Bhāgavatam)
fields.notes:
A brāhmaṇa named Raghunātha Paṇḍita, of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.79). The Lord heard him recite the Bhāgavatam at Varāhanagara on His way to Purī and named him Bhāgavatācārya (Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 5.110-121). In his book he calls Gadādhara his gurudeva. His śrīpāṭa, the Pāṭbāḍī, keeps his manuscripts.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Śvetamañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 195, 203).

Not the Bhāgavata Ācārya of Advaita's branch (Baḍa Śyāmadāsa, Prema-vilāsa 24) nor Bhāgavata dāsa, Bhūgarbha's companion.

fields.name: Śrī Madhu Paṇḍita
fields.place: Saibonā near Khaḍadaha (24 Parganas); Vaṁśīvaṭa, Vṛndāvana
fields.notes:
Disciple of Gadādhara Paṇḍita, living in Vṛndāvana; Śrī Gopīnātha of Vaṁśīvaṭa revealed Himself to him and he became His adhikārī; he installed Śrī Rādhā by Him (Bhakti-ratnākara 2.473-479; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Friend of Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya. Gave Śrīnivāsa Gopīnātha's garland when he left with the books. At Saibonā he set up Rādhā-Nanda-dulāl. The Rādhā-Gopīnātha deities are now in Jaipur. Not named in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Maṇḍalī sakhī (Caitanya-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā of Rāmāi Paṇḍita; Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā of Balarāma dāsa).

fields.name: Nayanānanda Miśra (Gadādhara's nephew)
fields.aka: Nayanānanda Ṭhākura, Miśra Nayana, Nayana Miśra, Dhruvānanda (earlier name, according to some), Nayanānanda Thakura / Misra
fields.notes:
Son of Vāṇīnātha, Gadādhara Paṇḍita's younger brother; brother of Hṛdayānanda. Gadādhara's dear disciple, «Miśra Nayana» of his branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.80). Gadādhara left him the deity of Gopīnātha, the small Gopīnātha he wore at his neck and his Gītā with a verse in Lord Caitanya's hand; his descendants serve them at Bharatpur (Prema-vilāsa). Married. Was at the Kheturī festival. His earlier name is said to have been Dhruvānanda (Padasamudra), but the Caitanya-caritāmṛta names a Dhruvānanda apart (Ādi 12.79).

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Nitya-mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 196, 207; Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 10).

A brāhmaṇa of Vṛndāvana of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.80); adhikārī of Śrī Govindadeva (Bhakti-ratnākara 13). Received Vīrabhadra Prabhu in Vṛndāvana (Bhakti-ratnākara 13.313-314). His disciple Haridāsa Paṇḍita told Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja to write the Caitanya-caritāmṛta. Guru-praṇālī: Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi → Gadādhara → Ananta Ācārya → Haridāsa Paṇḍita → Rādhākṛṣṇa Cakravartī.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Sudevī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 165).

The record said «an ancestor was Gopālī»: that belongs to Ananta Caṭṭarāja (Kaṇṭhābharaṇa), now in his own record.

fields.name: Haridāsa Paṇḍita (of Govindadeva)
fields.aka: Haridās Paṇḍit, Paṇḍita Haridāsa, Haridāsa Paṇḍita Gosāñi
fields.notes:
Beloved disciple of Ananta Ācārya, of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's line; head of the service of Śrī Govindadeva in Vṛndāvana, which Kṛṣṇadāsa Premī handed on to him (Sādhana-dīpikā 1). He told Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja to write the last pastimes of Lord Caitanya; the Caitanya-caritāmṛta praises his qualities (Ādi 8.54-65). Received Vīrabhadra Prabhu in Vṛndāvana (Bhakti-ratnākara 13.312-314). His disciple Rādhākṛṣṇa Cakravartī praises him in the Daśa-ślokī-bhāṣya as «an ornament of the Vārendra brāhmaṇas».

Not Haridāsa Ṭhākura (the record had that name as aka by mistake).

fields.place: Vṛndāvana; a Gadādhara Bhaṭṭa (Raṅgadevī) has his śrīpāṭa at Hanumānpur, Tailaṅga-deśa
fields.notes:
Disciple of Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, dear to Jīva Gosvāmī, a fine speaker on the Bhāgavatam (Bhaktamāla 23; Nāmāmṛta-samudra 271). Jīva sent him a letter with a verse after hearing his song; at the name of Vṛndāvana he fainted, then came to Vṛndāvana and surrendered to Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa.

The Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna first names a Gadādhara Bhaṭṭa who was Raṅgadevī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 165), of Hanumānpur in Tailaṅga-deśa, then this disciple of Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa as a second entry: perhaps two persons.

fields.name: Uddhava dāsa (of Gadādhara's branch)
fields.notes:
Of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.83); lived in Vṛndāvana by Pāvana-sarovara, devoted to Sanātana Gosvāmī. Went with Rūpa Gosvāmī to see Gopāla in Viṭṭhalanātha's house (Madhya 18.51); received Śrīnivāsa and Rāghava Gosvāmī in his āśrama (Bhakti-ratnākara 5.1333). Perhaps the poet of a song on Navadvīpa and the Kāzī.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: āveśa of Candrā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 112).

Not Uddhava dāsa the padakartā (Kṛṣṇakānta Majumdār, disciple of Rādhāmohana Ṭhākura), whose life was also in this record and is in his own record; nor Uddhava dāsa, disciple of Narahari Sarakāra and guru of Kavivallabha.

Of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.86); Gadādhara initiated him of his own accord on the autumn Kalpārambha and gave him Śrī Gaura-gopāla to serve; the Sāñjhī festival recalls it (Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 43). His disciple Nṛsiṁhavallabha founded the Mitra-ṭhākura family of Mayanāḍāla; his line at Kāndaḍā gave the Manoharaśāhī kīrtana singer Kālācānd Ṭhākura.

fields.name: Vallabha-caitanya dāsa
fields.notes: Disciple of Gadādhara Paṇḍita (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.82); sent by Lord Caitanya to preach in Vikramapura, where he installed Śrī Rādhāramaṇa. Married the daughter of his disciple Pūrṇacandra Bhaṭṭācārya; sons Rāmacandra, Mādhavendra, Mathurānātha and Rāmakṛṣṇa, and a daughter married to Vaidika Viṣṇudāsa (Nāmāmṛta-samudra 104; Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 18).

fields.name: Puruṣottama Jānā
fields.notes: Son of Gajapati Pratāparudra of Orissa; disciple of Gadādhara Paṇḍita (Bhakti-ratnākara 6.65). Sent two deities to Vṛndāvana, which became Rādhā and Lalitā of Madana-mohana, and then, told in a dream by Govinda, the «Lakṣmī» of the cakra-beḍa of Jagannātha, who became Rādhā of Govindadeva (Bhakti-ratnākara 6.63-72; Sādhana-dīpikā 128-129). The Lord's mercy on him as a boy: Caitanya-caritāmṛta Madhya 12.58-64.

Disciple of Bhūgarbha Gosvāmī, living in Vṛndāvana; one of those who told Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja to write the Caitanya-caritāmṛta («Kumudānanda Cakravartī, Premī Kṛṣṇadāsa», Ādi 8.69). According to the Sādhana-dīpikā (1) Rūpa Gosvāmī first gave him the service of Govinda, and he handed it on to Haridāsa Paṇḍita (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Kṛṣṇadāsa (Premī)»). The record had «Rūpa Gosvāmī (dīkṣā)» as guru and Haridāsa Paṇḍita as disciple: Rūpa gave him the service, not dīkṣā, and Haridāsa received the service from him.

fields.name: Dhruvānanda Brahmacārī
fields.notes:
A brāhmaṇa of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch: «the best of the branches, Dhruvānanda and Śrīdhara Brahmacārī» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.79). In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Lalitā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 152; Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 4). His descendants settled in the Burdwan district (Mahatā, Cānak, Māndār…), serving Govinda in each place.

The record of Nayanānanda Miśra says his earlier name was Dhruvānanda; the Caitanya-caritāmṛta names them apart. Not Dhruvānanda, disciple of Śyāmānanda, nor the Dhruvānanda of Kamalākara Pippalāi's line.

fields.name: Jayarāma Tarkālaṅkāra
fields.notes:
A Vārendra brāhmaṇa of the Pabna district; his father Jayadāsa was court paṇḍita of the Rāja of Puṭiyā. In old age he lived in Navadvīpa. A student of the famous logician Gadādhara (Bhaṭṭācārya), he wrote a detailed ṭīkā on Gadādhara's Śaktivāda (Viśvakoṣa VI, p. 682).

Not of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch: his teacher was the naiyāyika Gadādhara, so he was taken out of the Guru Paramparā (06-11-2026).

fields.name: Kavivallabha dāsa (author of the Rasakadamba)
fields.place: Aroḍā on the Karatoyā, near Mahāsthāna (Bogra)
fields.works: Rasakadamba (1520 Śaka); one song in the Padakalpataru (939)
fields.notes:
Father: Rājavallabha; mother: Vaiṣṇavī. His guru Uddhava dāsa was a disciple of Śrī Sarakāra Ṭhākura (Narahari). At the request of a brāhmaṇa named Mukuṭa Rāya he wrote the Rasakadamba in 1520 Śaka (1598); he lived at Aroḍā on the Karatoyā near Mahāsthāna, Bogra (Rasakadamba 997). One song of his, an ākṣepānurāga, is in the Padakalpataru (939) (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Kavivallabha dāsa»).

The record had the name «Kesivallabha» (a misreading) and the father «Bujavallabha». Not the Uddhava dāsa of Gadādhara's branch. Not Kavivallabha «Ākhariyā», disciple of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya.

fields.name: Kavivallabha «Ākhariyā» (disciple of Śrīnivāsa)
fields.notes: A disciple of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya: «Śrī Kavivallabha is the Prabhu's own servant … he wrote many books for the Prabhu: Ākhariyā» (Karṇānanda 2). For his beautiful handwriting he was called Ākhariyā; he copied many books for Śrīnivāsa (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Kavivallabha»). The record had the name «Kesivallabha» (a misreading).

fields.name: Ananta Caṭṭarāja (Śrī Kaṇṭhābharaṇa)
fields.notes: A brāhmaṇa of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch, named only by his title «Śrī Kaṇṭhābharaṇa» in the Caitanya-caritāmṛta (Ādi 12.80: «Gaṅgāmantrī, Māmu Ṭhākura, Kaṇṭhābharaṇa»); Yadunātha dāsa counts him in Gadādhara's line (Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 13). In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Gopālī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 196, 206).

fields.name: Gaṅgāmantrī
fields.notes:
Of Gadādhara Paṇḍita's branch, a resident of Orissa: «Gaṅgāmantrī, Māmu Ṭhākura, Kaṇṭhābharaṇa» (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 12.80). «I praise Gaṅgāmantrī, who delights in the joy of service, counselled by the Gaṅgā to make known the name and love» (Śākhā-nirṇayāmṛta 11). In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Candrikā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 196, 205) (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

The record said he was also called Māmu Ṭhākura or Kaṇṭhābharaṇa; the verse names three persons, and Kaṇṭhābharaṇa (Ananta Caṭṭarāja) has his own record; Yadunātha dāsa too keeps Māmu Ṭhākura apart.

A disciple of Śrī Sarakāra Ṭhākura (Narahari) and guru of Kavivallabha dāsa, who wrote the Rasakadamba in 1520 Śaka (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, «Kavivallabha dāsa»; Rasakadamba 997). Nothing else is known of him. Not Uddhava dāsa of Gadādhara's branch, nor the padakartā Uddhava dāsa, disciple of Rādhāmohana Ṭhākura.
